verified_title: UP-VLA: A Unified Understanding and Prediction Model for Embodied Agent
problem: Semantic VLM pretraining and future visual prediction provide complementary capabilities, but action-only adaptation can lose one or fail to preserve fine visual manipulation detail.
contribution: A unified Show-o/Phi1.5 policy combines language understanding,future image-token prediction and continuous action learning. Generated scene descriptions augment task prompts while training retains VQA and visual prediction objectives.
algorithm: Frozen CLIP-ViT encodes continuous understanding features; VQ/MagViT encodes discrete images. A1.3B Phi1.5/Show-o backbone predicts future tokens at corresponding current-image positions, rather than fully autoregressively rendering a separate goal image. Action queries attend to visual/language context and feed a small MAP-attention/linear policy head. Train text/image cross-entropy plus continuous-action MSE and gripper BCE, with task-specific loss sampling.
observations: Current images, instruction and the model's generated scene description; framework also depicts robot-pose input. Continuous understanding tokens and discrete prediction tokens have distinct encoders and attention masks. Generated descriptions can be semantically wrong and must not be treated as measured facts.
actions: Low-level continuous relative pose/action output and discrete gripper state through a small policy head. Exact hardware control frequency,chunk horizon and detailed axis convention NOT_EXTRACTED; do not infer them from CALVIN defaults.
embodiment_and_data: Pretrained Show-o512×512 1.3B; Bridge25000robot demonstrations for prediction andLLaVA665kVQA for understanding. Initial20ksteps/batch64,followed by target action learning. PhysicalFrankaPanda uses>2000demonstrations across6skills includinggrasp/place,cables,buttons anddrawers,from manualteleoperation andscripted block-grasp data.
experiments: CALVINABC-to-D andABCD-to-D report five-task chain success/length. Hardware evaluates seen/unseen/precision tasks with20attempts per task. Controlled ablations removeMMU,Bridge pretraining,visual prediction or scene-description conditioning. Original external baselines are mostly copied benchmark results; starred variants are locally reproduced.
baselines: RT-1,DiffusionPolicy,RoboFlamingo,3D-VLA,UniPi,SuSIE,GR-1,3DDiffuserActor,and matched UP-VLA-RT2/Phi-withoutMMU. The matched controls have different prompting/objectives, so this is a combined training mechanism comparison.

limitations: Future imagery can hallucinate appearance and descriptions can name objects incorrectly. Some semantic ablations improve seen-task success while reducing transfer. Hardware data and simulated chain success do not establish bimanual cloth skill. Runtime,memory and precise action schema are insufficiently specified for direct reproduction; the1.3B model size alone does not qualify NX.
code_and_license: No pinned implementation,weights or code/data licenses inspected; no execution. Show-o/Phi/Bridge/LLaVA components require independent terms review before copying or redistribution.
hardware_adaptation: COMPARE a compact ACT student's training with future-feature and description supervision separately. Keep hallucinated captions/predicted images separate from actual camera evidence. Use real source-bound episodes with calibrated target action/state names and preserve controller settings. Measure end-to-end latency, including text generation, before an NX deployment claim.
